What this is

This file is the review of one working session, in the format the session built, read by the code the session added.

leela/blocks/canvas/app.py:page wrote the page you are reading. It read this file, asked git for the diff this file names, and rendered both.

Give Leela one document that holds a goal, its plan, its research, its code and its questions, and one page that shows all five to a reviewer on a phone.

Words

Read this table first. Every later section uses these words and no others.

wordmeans
brickone part of the document: a fence or a comment wrap. A code cell, a question, a goal, a task, a clipping.
proseordinary markdown between bricks. It carries no markup of its own.
regionthe bricks under one heading. The headings make the regions, so nobody writes one.
basketthe exact list of bricks that one question sends to the model.
bundleone unit of change. It claims a region, names a goal, and owns a list of files.
snippeta brick that cites code out of a file. It keeps no copy of that code.
slota diff brick with no body. It states which diff it wants; Leela fills it.
libraryan installed package of components. leela_bricks is the first one.
needswhat a component's wiring imports. Read off the code, never written by hand.
patathe retired name for this work. Sanskrit for the cloth a scroll painting is made on. The name now is canvas.

Why it helps

A diff tells a reviewer which lines moved. It cannot answer the three questions a reviewer brings to a change.

  1. What was this change supposed to do?
  2. Did it do that?
  3. Did anything else move that nobody meant to move?

The intent is in the document, not in the diff. So the document states the intent, the diff states the fact, and coverage compares them. Its unmet list is a claim with no change behind it, and its unclaimed list is a change with no claim behind it. Neither list can come out of a diff tool, which holds one of the two sets.

This page shows that comparison at the top, as chips, before any code.

Why can a diff tool not report unclaimed on its own?

unclaimed is the difference between two sets. A diff tool holds the files that moved. It does not hold the files a change promised to touch, which sit in each bundle's paths. A finding needs both sets.

The document

done
Worth: the file every other part reads

A canvas is a markdown file. Prose stays prose. A brick is a fence or a comment wrap. Every markdown reader therefore shows the file, and git shows a useful diff. The ast module reads the dataflow between code bricks off the code itself.

doc:docs/canvas.mdfile:leela/blocks/nb/nb.py

Two brick shapes, and the shape follows the content. Code goes in a fence, because a fence is how markdown holds code. A goal or a task goes in a comment wrap, because a reader should see the words and not the markup.

A fence holds what markdown already knows how to show, so a code cell stays a code block. A comment wrap holds what a reader should read as prose, so a goal shows its words and not its markup. KINDS is the whole vocabulary, and a document with a word outside it does not parse.

order reads the graph rather than storing it. defs_of asks the code what it defines, and reads_of asks what it reads. order joins two bricks when one defines what the other reads.

order reads the dependency from the code. _owners says which brick defines each name, and b.reads says which names a brick needs, so no person draws an edge. On a cycle the visit stops and the document order stands, so a plan with a loop in it still opens.

The basket

done
Worth: what a question in the document may read

A question names its own scope, its pins and its budget. resolve returns the exact bricks, and each one carries the reason it is there. render emits the cells that ramabana's compact_notebook_context already knows how to shed.

leela/blocks/canvas/context.py
pkg:ramabanafile:leela/blocks/nb/nb.py

A notebook sends every brick above the question. A pin sends the two that matter, wherever they sit. An audit belongs to the question at the top of the page and the one at the bottom, and to nothing between.

A question states its own rule, and the rule is four fields. scope gathers the first set, pins add what the scope missed, and mutes remove what it caught. An unknown scope becomes page rather than an error, so a typed attribute cannot stop a document from opening.

The budget sheds the least useful brick first, not the oldest, and never a pin or the goal. Each Item carries the why that put it there. A reviewer can therefore see which bricks the budget dropped.

The change

done
Worth: all of the review step

A bundle claims a region, names a goal and owns a list of files. coverage compares the claim with the diff. Leela reads state off the document, and no one sets it by hand. review, value and pr are three views over the same file.

Leela derives the state of a change. A bundle reaches done once every task reaches done and every claimed file moved. No one writes that word into the file.

state reads the word off the document. One blocked task blocks the change, and every task done with every claimed file moved makes it done. files_ok treats an absent diff as no evidence, so a change nobody has diffed yet does not read as work not started.

The comparison a diff tool cannot make:

matched is a claim the diff confirms, unmet is a claim with nothing behind it, and unclaimed is a file that moved with no claim on it. A claim is a glob, so leela/blocks/canvas/* covers every file the change touched in that folder without naming one of them.

The page

Leela now assembles this page. The tool that used to do it picks a file and prints a line.

page fills the slots, counts the files and writes the HTML in one call. It returns the file list and the unclaimed list, so a caller sees the finding without opening the page.

A diff brick with no body is a slot. It says which paths it wants and which two commits to compare. place_diff calls git once per slot and replaces the slot with one brick a file. place_diff marks a brick no bundle claims, and the page shows a warning on it.

place_diff reads the request off the brick. A diff brick with a body is content, and is left alone, so a pasted diff is never overwritten. Each slot becomes one brick a file, and a file no bundle claims gets claimed=no, which the page shows as a warning.

The page folds anything longer than a phone screen. A diff body scrolls sideways inside its own box, and a long line therefore never widens the page.

The renderer folds a diff longer than a phone screen, and the summary still names the file and the counts. It drops the git headers a reader does not need. It writes no script, so the fold is <details> and the page works with JavaScript turned off.

The library

done
Worth: the palette, with no second process

The palette used to be an HTTP call to a second server. It is now an entry-point group. A library answers four questions: its manifest, one brick, that brick's wiring, and its own routes. An HTTP host answers the same four, and it stays for a library nobody installed.

docs/bricks.mdextensions/bricks/*leela/blocks/canvas/bricks.pytests/fixtures/*
pkg:leela-bricksdoc:docs/bricks.md

The four questions are the whole contract. A library that answers them needs to know nothing about Leela, and Leela needs to know nothing about the library.

A library answers four questions and knows nothing about Leela. manifest lists its components, find returns one, wire returns the code that fills its ports, and mount puts its own routes on the app it is handed. manifest is read in process, so the palette needs no second server.

needs comes from the wiring's own imports. A component cannot claim a dependency its code does not import, and cannot hide one it does.

needs reads the imports out of the wiring text. A component cannot claim a dependency its code does not import, and cannot hide one it does. The standard library is dropped, so the list is what a person must install before the cell will run.

A library never writes its own name into a src string. LIB comes from __name__. Renaming the package therefore renames every src it serves. This is why extensions/bricks extracted with no code change. Eight files moved, and the only edit added a Registry to bricks.py.

The wiring

CAPS must name exactly what the routes read off ctx. The canvas block reads two things: the file system, and the model.

CAPS is a promise about ctx, and Leela checks it. A route that reads a capability the block did not declare fails at load, not at the request that reads it.

What running it found

Two faults survived every reading of the merged block. Running it end to end found both.

The editor lost typing in a code brick. An insert anywhere in the document runs cvSync, which keeps the element and hands it a new brick object. The textarea then wrote to an object the document no longer held, and the next flush read the older body. cvEdit writes through to cvBrick(id), and cvKeepEdits carries an edited body across the sync. The browser test in tests/test_web_slow.py returns the empty body on the code before the fix.

The context basket has a route and no panel. /canvas/context returns the exact bricks one question will send, each with the rule that chose it, and 51 tests cover the model. The merged editor has no control that opens it. Neither branch built one, because the canvas branch built the editor and this side built the basket. t14 above records the gap.

  • [x]Fix the stale-object write and add the browser test that reproduces it.me
  • [ ]Give the basket a panel: a control on an `ask` brick that shows what the question will send.me

explain.md hands ste.md to the model that drafts a snippet. A drafted sentence therefore met the rules, and a hand-written one did not. Three patterns carried most of the weight. A sentence states a thing and then restates its opposite. A closing line reverses the sentence before it. A passive clause drops the doer. ste.md bans all three by name.

What the score still reports is not slop. A package name reads as a coinage. A bold UI label reads as emphasis. A list of three parallel clauses reads as a long sentence. ste.md permits the third by name, and the first two are the words the product uses.

docs/screenshots/canvas-prose-goals.png shows both goals on this page, and canvas-prose-review.png and canvas-prose-phone.png show this section on a desktop and on a phone. Leela drew all three from this file.

Eighteen tests failed on this branch before the review, and none of them for a reason the branch introduced. Four were the environment: no brick library installed, no generated icon, and no venv on PATH. Two guards read a route surface that grows with whatever library the machine has, so they now measure Leela's own. Three tests compared a liveness that a zombie also reports, or a PNG that Pillow re-encodes between versions.

One was a fault in the code. TurnRunner._reap read Thread.is_alive alone, which is False before a thread starts as well as after it ends. start publishes the pending turn and only then starts its worker. A request arriving in that window reaped a live turn and won acceptance. That is the second turn _pending exists to refuse. worker.ident tells an unstarted thread from a finished one, and two tests in tests/blocks/test_agent_threads.py hold each half.

The review

done
Worth: the branch being safe to merge

Four faults were critical and six were high. Every route that took a path read, ran or overwrote whatever it named. A canvas ran its Python in the web process. A frame had this page's origin, and the markdown writer let a URL close an attribute. The wheel excluded the files the client read at request time.

leela/blocks/agent/models.pyleela/blocks/canvas/*leela/blocks/debug/*leela/blocks/drive/*leela/blocks/editor/app.pyleela/blocks/pipelines/*leela/blocks/runtime/*leela/blocks/search/search.pyleela/blocks/vars/app.pyleela/blocks/vault/jobs.pyleela/blocks/workflows/*leela/static/lee-canvas.jsmedia/e2e/*tests/test_agent.pytests/test_agent_slow.pytests/test_git_folder.pytests/test_kernels_ipymini.pytests/test_pipelines.pytests/test_seams.pytests/test_web_slow.pytests/test_workflows.pytools/build_ide_js.pyuv.lock
doc:docs/canvas.mdpkg:kundapkg:pullup

The path gate is one function, canvas_path, and every source and destination passes it. A canvas runs in a kunda kernel now, and only after somebody says it may: opening a document draws it and executes nothing. Both frames are sandboxed with allow-scripts and no same-origin. The client is a committed bundle, leela/static/lee-canvas.js, built from the order ui.FILES states.

The seams cost the widest change. test_seams.py guarded eleven libraries and not kunda or pullup, the two Leela composes most. Eight reaches into their private names went uncounted. runtime/support.py re-exported almost the whole of kunda's support half. core/envs.py went straight to kunda for three of the same names, so clean_env had two spellings. Fifteen call sites in ten modules now import from kunda directly. That is why this change reaches blocks with nothing to do with a canvas.

Kunda's execute(timeout=) does not return on a busy loop. while True: pass sat past two hundred seconds under it, and interrupt stopped the same cell in milliseconds. So KernelRuntime holds the bound itself: wait, interrupt, wait again, then shut the kernel down and start another. A cell that calls os._exit takes its kernel and nothing else.

Three steps, because each one can fail on its own. interrupt is what actually stops a cell, and the wait around it is what makes the timeout real. Giving up on the kernel costs the namespace, which is the whole reason a kernel is worth having.

The gate compares the resolved path against the root it must be under, so a relative path cannot walk up out of it. With a folder open the workspace decides; with none, which is the spike and the tests, the canvas directory does.

  • [x]Gate every route's paths, both source and destination.me
  • [x]Run a canvas in a kernel, with a timeout, an interrupt and explicit trust.me
  • [x]Sandbox both frames, and refuse a URL or an attribute that is script.me
  • [x]Ship the client in the wheel, and hold it with a test against a built one.me
  • [x]Make `pytest -m slow` finish, and fix what running it found.me

pytest -m slow was OOM-killed a third of the way in and reported nothing. Not the tests it could never run, and not the ones above them that pass in seconds. Two suites resolved a real local model, because its bundle happened to be cached on the machine. The trace reads plainly. No engine sat at 290MB. The first took it to 871MB and the second to 3.1GB. Each streaming test after that added two to three gigabytes while the Python heap stayed flat, so the growth was native and inside the engines. A browser test drives painting and panels, and needs no model at all. The suite now runs 80 tests in 4m29s, peaking at 967MB.

Five monkeypatches aimed at Leela's re-exports rather than the name the library reads. kunda.pool imports Kernel into its own namespace, so the fakes were ignored. One test failed and one hung on a real kernel that never signalled. One assertion expected read_only to drop the delegate tools by default. shalya moved that to a block= the caller passes, and both production call sites pass it, so the test was red while the behaviour was right. One test read a notebook out of an untracked folder a real kernel had written into the checkout. Three counted the buttons in a bar that gained a fourth.

The gate asked whether the bundle was cached and not whether the machine could hold it. One engine climbs to 12.2GB and a run that reached 13.4GB died with 3.1GB nominally free, so the number is 16000 and the comment above it says where that came from.

examples/canvas/making-a-block.canvas.md +79 -0
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@+---+title: Making a block+mode: make+---++# Making a block++This document holds the software and the note about it. The code below is what a library puts in+its own `data.py`, and the component under it reads that data. Both of them run here.++```canvas code id=m1+from datetime import date, timedelta++def burndown(start, days, done_per_day):+ "Points left on each day, from a start and a rate."+ left, out = start, []+ for i in range(days):+ left = max(0, left - done_per_day)+ out.append({'day': (date(2026, 9, 1) + timedelta(days=i)).strftime('%d %b'), 'left': left})+ return out++plan = burndown(180, 12, 16)+labels = [p['day'] for p in plan]+left = [p['left'] for p in plan]+```++```canvas brick id=m2 src=leela_bricks:viz.series emit_point=point+bind labels = labels+bind series = [{'name': 'points left', 'values': left}]+prop height = 240+```++```canvas code id=m3+point = {'label': labels[0], 'value': left[0]}+lands = next((p['day'] for p in plan if p['left'] == 0), 'not in this window')+```++```canvas data id=m4+bind text = f"On the plan as written it lands **{lands}**. examples/canvas/pricing-a-run.canvas.md +69 -0
@@ -0,0 +1,69 @@+---+title: Pricing a run+mode: make+---++# Pricing a run++An agent run costs four numbers and one multiplication. Every argument about the cost is an+argument about one of the four. Put the four in a cell, and the argument becomes editable.++```canvas code id=p1+in_tokens = 18_000+out_tokens = 2_400+runs_a_day = 400+prices = {'Opus 5': (15, 75), 'Sonnet 5': (3, 15), 'Haiku 4.5': (0.8, 4)}+```++```canvas code id=p2+def cost(model):+ i, o = prices[model]+ return in_tokens/1e6*i + out_tokens/1e6*o++rows = [{'label': m, 'per_request': round(cost(m), 5), 'monthly': round(cost(m)*runs_a_day*30, 2)}+ for m in prices]+rows+```++```canvas brick id=p3 src=leela_bricks:thrifty.costs emit_row=picked+bind rows = rows+prop height = 220+```++```canvas code id=p4+picked = rows[-1]+```++```canvas data id=p5+bind text = f"**{picked['label']}** at this shape of request is ${picked['per_request']} a call and ${picked['monthly']:,.0f} a month at {runs_a_day} runs a day. The cheapest option is {(min(rows, key=lambda r: r['monthly'])['monthly']/picked['monthly']*100):.0f}% of that."+```++Click a row. `picked` changes, and the sentence below binds to `picked`, which changes it too.++## The knob that actually matters++```canvas sim id=p6+prop height = 120+const draw = () => {+ root.innerHTML = `<div class="row"><label style="width:140px">runs a day</label>+ <input type=range min=50 max=5000 step=50 id=r><b id=v></b></div>`;+ const r = root.querySelector('#r');+ r.value = props.runs_a_day ?? 400;+ const show = () => root.querySelector('#v').textContent = r.value;+ r.oninput = show; r.onchange = () => { show(); emit('runs_a_day', +r.value); }; show();+};+```++```canvas brick id=p7 src=leela_bricks:viz.series+bind labels = [r['label'] for r in rows]+bind series = [{'name': 'monthly $', 'values': [r['monthly'] for r in rows]}]+prop height = 240+```++Every model here prices an output token at four to five times an input token. examples/canvas/tunnelling.canvas.md +69 -0
@@ -0,0 +1,69 @@+---+title: Tunnelling+mode: learn+---++# Tunnelling++A particle with less energy than a barrier still turns up on the other side. It goes through the+barrier rather than over the top. The amplitude inside the barrier decays instead of oscillating.+If the barrier ends before the decay finishes, the remaining amplitude keeps going.++The simulation below integrates the one-dimensional Schrödinger equation in the frame, at forty+steps a screen refresh. It computes every frame as it draws.++```canvas code id=q1+barrier = 1.02+width = 6+```++```canvas brick id=q2 src=leela_bricks:learn.wavepacket emit_transmission=transmission+bind barrier = barrier+bind width = width+prop height = 300+```++```canvas sim id=q3+prop height = 130+const draw = () => {+ root.innerHTML = `<div class="row"><label style="width:130px">barrier ×E</label>+ <input type=range min=0.9 max=2 step=0.02 id=b><b id=bv></b></div>+ <div class="row"><label style="width:130px">width</label>+ <input type=range min=2 max=30 step=1 id=w><b id=wv></b></div>`;+ const b = root.querySelector('#b'), w = root.querySelector('#w');+ b.value = props.barrier ?? 1.02; w.value = props.width ?? 6;+ const show = () => { root.querySelector('#bv').textContent = (+b.value).toFixed(2);+ root.querySelector('#wv').textContent = w.value; };+ b.onchange = () => { show(); emit('barrier', +b.value); };+ w.onchange = () => { show(); emit('width', +w.value); };+ b.oninput = show; w.oninput = show; show();+};+```++```canvas code id=q4+transmission = 0.0+kappa = round((2 * max(1e-6, (barrier - 1)) * 0.245) ** 0.5, 4)+predicted = round(2.718281828 ** (-2 * kappa * width) * 100, 2)+```++```canvas data id=q5+bind text = f"At {barrier:.2f}× the packet energy over {width} cells, the decay constant κ is {kappa} and the crude estimate exp(−2κa) is **{predicted}%**. The simulation is measuring **{transmission*100:.1f}%**."+```++Drag the barrier up. The transmitted lobe on the right disappears long before the barrier reaches+twice the packet energy. Tunnelling falls exponentially with both the height and the width. A+barrier half again as thick therefore leaks much less than half as much.++```canvas ask id=q6+explain tunnelling+```++```canvas video id=q7 src=Ltni6c1lC4c+Sixty Symbols explains quantum tunnelling aloud.+```++<!--canvas quiz id=q8-->+1. Why does doubling the barrier width cost more than doubling its height+2. What is the packet doing inside the barrier, if it is not oscillating+3. Where does the reflected part of the packet go+<!--/canvas-->
extensions/bricks/README.md +57 -0
@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@+# leela-bricks++Components a canvas document can embed. Ten of them, in four groups.++A canvas document embeds one with a `brick` brick:++```markdown+```canvas brick id=b1 src=leela_bricks:viz.series emit_point=point+bind labels = list(cycle.index)+bind series = [{'name': 'days to clear', 'values': list(cycle.values)}]+prop height = 240+```+```++## Install++```sh+pip install -e extensions/bricks+```++Leela finds it through the `leela.bricks` entry point. Leela needs no other configuration, and+`LEELA_BRICK_HOST` serves only a library nobody installed. See+[docs/bricks.md](../../docs/bricks.md).++## What a brick declares++`Registry.brick(name, title, group, ports, emits, wire, height, doc)`. `ports` name what the component draws+from. `emits` name what a click writes back into the document's namespace. `wire` is the code+that fills the ports.++`wire` gives `needs`, and nobody declares it. `needs` is the top-level packages the snippet+imports, minus the standard library. Six of the ten need nothing. The four under `panchanga` and+`thrifty` each import a domain package, and a document without that package reads its ports over+`data.remote_wire` instead.++`src` is `LIB:name`, and `LIB` is this package's own module name. It is never a literal. A brick+therefore cannot claim a package it no longer lives in.++## Routes++`serve.connect(app, page=None)` registers seven routes on any Starlette or FastHTML app, and it+imports nothing from that app. Leela mounts the routes in its own process, and no second server+runs.++| route | is |+|---|---|+| `/bricks` | the gallery |+| `/bricks/manifest.json` | every brick, its ports and its emits |+| `/bricks/f/{name}` | one component, as a frame |+| `/bricks/wire/{name}` | the snippet, and the call that reads the ports remotely |+| `/bricks/data/{name}` | the ports, filled by running the snippet here |+| `/bricks/js`, `/bricks/css` | the drawing |++## Extracting it++This directory is the package. `pip install extensions/bricks` works anywhere, because nothing in+the package imports Leela. To move it to its own repository, use `git mv` and add a remote.

Change the cut in `bands`, and it moves with everything else.++```canvas ask id=q-fix scope=upstream budget=8000+`cycle_days` was not a column. @@ -0,0 +1,118 @@+"""Working in a canvas: a markdown document whose bricks run, bind and hand values back.++Read this before editing a canvas.++## What a canvas is++Not a notebook and not a page. One markdown file where prose is prose and everything else is a+brick, and where each brick recomputes when what it reads moves. The document is the program and+the note about the program at once.++## The file++`*.canvas.md`. Optional YAML frontmatter carries `title` and `mode`. Prose between bricks is a+`text` brick and needs no markup of its own.++A brick that is opaque to markdown is a fence:++ ```canvas <kind> id=<id> key=value ...+ <body>+ ```++A brick whose body is markdown a plain renderer should still show is a comment wrap:++ <!--canvas <kind> id=<id>-->+ Ordinary **markdown**.+ <!--/canvas-->++Fenced kinds: `code`, `ask`, `brick`, `sim`, `data`, `pdf`, `video`.+Wrapped kinds: `reply`, `note`, `quiz`.++A non-code brick body holds directives, one per line, and nothing else:++ bind <port> = <expression>+ prop <key> = <value>++A code brick body is the code, kept exactly. Directives are never read out of it.++## Bindings, and what runs++Code bricks share one namespace. They run in dependency order derived from the AST, not document+order, so a cell may be written above the cell it needs. A canvas stores no outputs: opening one+runs it.++`bind port = expression` evaluates the expression against that namespace and hands the result to+the brick. When a name the expression reads moves, the binding is resolved again. A binding that+raises reports on the brick rather than blanking it.++`data` is the brick that makes prose live: `bind text = f"..."` renders the result as markdown.+Prefer it over writing a number into prose. A number written by hand is wrong the moment anything+above it changes.++## Emits: what a component hands back++A component brick emits. `emit_<port>=<name>` in its attributes says which name in the namespace a+port writes to. Clicking a funnel bar, a rasi or an organelle sets that name and reruns everything+that reads it. A component is an input as much as an output.++Two components in one document must not write to the same name unless they are meant to.++## Components, bricks and sketches++`brick` embeds a component from a package: `src=lego.bricks:viz.series`. The package declares the+ports, what it emits, and the code that fills it. Take that code rather than writing your own:+`canvas_wire(name)` returns it, `canvas_insert` puts it in the document as an ordinary code brick,+and `canvas_bind` points the ports at what it defined. The wiring stays visible in the file.++`sim` is a component written in the document itself. Its body is JavaScript with `root`, `props`+and `emit` in scope, and nothing else. Promote one into a package without changing a line.++## Your tools: the ports into the document++| tool | does |+|---|---|+| `canvas_read` | the document as it stands: every brick, its kind, its bindings, what it defines |+| `canvas_insert` | a new brick at a position. `after=<id>` or `at=<index>` |+| `canvas_replace` | rewrite one brick, by id |+| `canvas_remove` | take a brick out, by id |+| `canvas_bind` | point one port of one brick at an expression |+| `canvas_run` | run a code brick and let the dataflow settle |+| `canvas_answer` | prose written back into the document, attached to the question that asked for it |+| `canvas_values` | read names out of the live namespace |++Every one goes through the same function the person's own edits go through. There is no second+path into the document, and nothing else you can reach touches it.++## How to work++Read before you write. `canvas_read` costs one call and tells you what ids exist, what each cell+defines and what every binding reads. Editing by guess breaks bindings that were fine.++Answer where the question was asked. `canvas_answer(of=<ask id>)` puts the reply under the ask and+replaces the previous one rather than stacking. Prose that belongs in the document goes in the+document, not only in the reply.++Change the smallest thing. A wrong number is usually one binding, not a rewritten section. Rewrite+a selection with `canvas_replace` only for the span you were given.++Insert code that runs. A code brick arrives to be run: it runs where it lands, and anything bound+to the names it defines resolves. Do not insert a cell that needs a second call to be useful.++Bind rather than paste. If a value already exists in the namespace, bind to it. Pasting the value+makes a document that was live into a document that was true once.++Name what you emit. When you add a component whose clicks should drive something, set+`emit_<port>` to a name the document already reads, or add the cell that reads it in the same turn.++Prefer a brick to a paragraph about a brick. A canvas is for showing the thing.++## The trail, and where a question came from++A question carries where it was asked from: the brick, and the text that was selected in it. The+last dozen of those are the trail, and they arrive with the turn. Use them. "Why is that one+cheaper" resolves against the row that was clicked, and asking the person to repeat themselves+wastes the context you were given.++A selection is a span, not a topic. Rewriting one rewrites that span and leaves the rest of the+brick alone.+"""

A fence inside a longer fence is an example of one, not one.&quot;+ lines, i, prose, out = text.split(&#x27;\n&#x27;), 0, [], []+ def flush():+ for part in _prose_parts(&#x27;\n&#x27;.join(prose)): out.append((&#x27;text&#x27;, &#x27;&#x27;, part))+ prose.clear()+ def upto(j, shut, keep):+ body = []+ while j &lt; len(lines) and not shut(lines[j]): body.append(lines[j]); j += 1+ if keep and j &lt; len(lines): body.append(lines[j])+ return j, body+ while i &lt; len(lines):+ line = lines[i]+ if (m := FENCE.match(line)):+ flush()+ end = _shut(m[1])+ i, body = upto(i + 1, lambda l: end.match(l), False)+ out.append((m[2], m[3], &#x27;\n&#x27;.join(body) + (&#x27;\n&#x27; if body else &#x27;&#x27;)))+ elif (m := TICKS.match(line)):+ end = _shut(m[1])+ prose.append(line)+ i, body = upto(i + 1, lambda l: end.match(l), True)+ prose.extend(body)+ elif (m := WRAP.match(line)):+ flush()+ attr = [line[m.end():]]+ while not SHUT_TAG.search(attr[-1]) and i + 1 &lt; len(lines): # a long attribute list wraps+ i += 1+ attr.append(lines[i])+ i, body = upto(i + 1, lambda l: l.strip() == SHUT, False)+ out.append((m[1], SHUT_TAG.sub(&#x27;&#x27;, &#x27; &#x27;.join(attr)), &#x27;\n&#x27;.join(body) + (&#x27;\n&#x27; if body else &#x27;&#x27;)))+ else:+ prose.append(line); i += 1; continue+ i += 1+ flush()+ return out</code></pre></div></details></figure><p>Headings are the regions of the document. The same list draws the panel+and builds the prompt. What a person sees is what the model gets.</p>+<p>Four rules, in order. The goal goes in first. Then each pin. A silent drop is worse, because the person still believes the pin is+there.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/context.py</b> &middot; resolve</figcaption><details><summary>resolve (29 lines)</summary><div class="in"><pre><code class="lang-python">def resolve(+ doc, # the document+ bid, # which brick asks+ spec=None, # the rule, else the one the brick carries+ values=None, # `{brick id: output text}` from the live namespace+ lookup=None, # `lookup(ref)` for a pin the document does not own+ extra=(), # items the host adds, such as live variables+):+ &quot;The exact basket for question `bid`, in the order the model reads it.&quot;+ b = doc.by_id(bid)+ if b is None: raise KeyError(bid)+ spec = spec or spec_of(b)+ mutes, items, seen = set(spec.mutes), [], {b.id}+ def take(x, why, pinned=False):+ if x.id in seen or x.id in mutes: return+ if not (t := body_text(x, values, doc)).strip(): return+ seen.add(x.id)+ items.append(Item(ref=x.id, kind=x.kind, label=_label(x), text=t, why=why,+ region=x.region, mode=x.mode, pinned=pinned or x.mode == &#x27;keep&#x27;))+ if spec.goal and (g := doc.goal_for(bid)) is not None and g.id not in mutes: take(g, &#x27;goal&#x27;, True)+ for r in spec.pins:+ if r in mutes: continue+ if _is_ref(r): items.append(_ref_item(r, lookup))+ elif (x := doc.by_id(r)) is not None: take(x, &#x27;pin&#x27;, True)+ else: items.append(Item(ref=r, kind=&#x27;missing&#x27;, label=r, text=&#x27;&#x27;, why=&#x27;pin&#x27;, pinned=True,+ clipped=True))+ for x in members(doc, b, spec.scope): take(x, spec.scope)+ items += list(extra)+ return _fit(items, spec.budget)</code></pre></div></details></figure><p>A scope gives the first set of bricks. <code>page</code> is the notebook rule. <code>region</code> is the section that+you work in. <code>upstream</code> is what the question reads from.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/context.py</b> &middot; members</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python">def members(doc, b, scope):+ &quot;The bricks a scope offers, before pins, mutes and the budget.&quot;+ if scope == &#x27;none&#x27;: return L()+ at = doc.index(b.id)+ if at is None: at = len(doc)+ if scope == &#x27;page&#x27;: return L(doc.bricks[:at])+ if scope == &#x27;doc&#x27;: return L(x for x in doc.bricks if x.id != b.id)+ if scope == &#x27;region&#x27;: return L(x for x in doc.in_region(b.region) if x.id != b.id)+ return upstream(doc.bricks, b.id)</code></pre></figure><p>The budget cuts the list. Pins and `keep` never drop; `discard` goes first, then the oldest `auto`.&quot;+ if not budget: return items+ total = sum(i.chars + WRAP for i in items)+ if total &lt;= budget: return items+ order = sorted((i for i, it in enumerate(items) if not it.pinned),+ key=lambda i: (items[i].mode != &#x27;discard&#x27;, i))+ drop, n = set(), 0+ while total &gt; budget and n &lt; len(order):+ total -= items[order[n]].chars + WRAP+ drop.add(order[n])+ n += 1+ kept = [it for i, it in enumerate(items) if i not in drop]+ if sum(i.chars + WRAP for i in kept) &gt; budget and kept:+ share = max(200, budget // max(1, len(kept)) - WRAP)+ kept = [replace(it, text=it.text[:share] + &#x27;\n…&#x27;, clipped=True) if it.chars &gt; share else it+ for it in kept]+ return kept</code></pre></figure><p>The markup is <code>&lt;cell&gt;</code> with a <code>compact</code> attribute. The numbers

Which part of this session would be hardest to rebuild from the diff alone?

The intent. Every line of code on this branch is in the diff, and none of the four contributes lines is. A reader of the diff can see that coverage subtracts two sets. Only the document says which set was a promise.

Checks

  • [x]125 canvas tests pass, 1 skipped: the example that wires itself from a component host, with none running. The browser test needs `-m slow`.me
  • [x]`leela_bricks` installs from `extensions/bricks` and the resolver finds all ten of its components.me
  • [x]Leela writes this page from this file, with a real git diff in the slot.me
